package.title: What Happens When You Take Creatine
package.phrase: what happens when you take creatine
package.opener: What happens when you take creatine? Almost all of it is absorbed, and about 95% of the body's creatine is stored in the muscles, where it helps recharge their energy (ATP) in short, hard efforts. A review of 100 studies found small gains, mostly in short, repeated efforts, not in running or swimming. In the first days the scale can go up 1 to 3 kg, mostly water. Creatine raises creatinine on a blood test (by about 0.14 mg/dL in two 2026 reviews), which can look like kidney trouble; trials in healthy adults found no kidney harm, but that is not proof of safety for everyone.

sources.label: Kreider RB et al. International Society of Sports Nutrition position stand: safety and efficacy of creatine supplementation in exercise, sport, and medicine. J Int Soc Sports Nutr 2017;14:18
sources.note: 'The majority of creatine is found in skeletal muscle (~95%)'; 'absorption into the blood is nearly 100%'; the free energy of PCr 'can be used as a buffer to resynthesize ATP ... particularly during maximal effort anaerobic sprint-type exercise'; 'About 1-2% of intramuscular creatine is degraded into creatinine'. Several authors have ties to creatine makers (declared).

sources.label: Antonio J et al. Common questions and misconceptions about creatine supplementation: what does the scientific evidence really show? J Int Soc Sports Nutr 2021;18:13
sources.note: 'the most common adverse effect of creatine supplementation is water retention in the early stages (first several days)'; loading 'typically results in a 1-3 kg increase in body mass, mostly attributable to net body water retention'; 'one must exercise caution when using blood creatinine ... in individuals who ... supplement with creatine'; the 1998 kidney case was a man 'who had kidney disease for 8 years'. Several authors have ties to creatine makers (declared).

sources.label: Branch JD. Effect of creatine supplementation on body composition and performance: a meta-analysis. Int J Sport Nutr Exerc Metab 2003;13:198-226
sources.note: 100 placebo-controlled studies. 'Small, but significant' effects, greater for repetitive-bout tasks of 30 s or less; creatine 'does not appear to be effective in improving running and swimming performance'.

sources.label: Raihan FA, Supriyanta A. Creatine supplementation and kidney function in healthy, physically active adults: a systematic review and meta-analysis. Int Urol Nephrol, 17 Nov 2026
sources.note: 12 trials. Creatine 'raised serum creatinine by 12.10 µmol/L (≈ 0.14 mg/dL)'; the evidence 'is compatible with no effect of creatine on kidney function in healthy adults but ... does not establish renal safety'. No industry ties.

sources.label: de Souza Almeida A et al. Impact of creatine supplementation on kidney health: a systematic review and meta-analysis. Int Urol Nephrol 2026;58:5423-34
sources.note: 26 studies, 1036 people. Serum creatinine up 0.14 mg/dL; no difference when filtration was measured directly (Cr-EDTA); 'These findings likely reflect altered creatinine metabolism rather than kidney injury'.

sources.label: Lak M et al. Does creatine cause hair loss? A 12-week randomized controlled trial. J Int Soc Sports Nutr 2025
sources.note: 38 resistance-trained men completed 12 weeks; 'no significant differences in DHT levels, DHT-to-testosterone ratio, or hair growth parameters between the creatine and placebo groups'. Some authors have ties to supplement makers (declared).

lines.text: Your scale jumps... is it fat?
What? I only started creatine this week!
Almost all of me gets into your blood.
And ninety-five percent of me heads for your muscles.
A bit more power for short, hard bursts.
A long run? Studies say it barely helps.
A little of me breaks down into creatinine.
Your blood test shows more of it. Looks like kidney trouble!
But in trials with healthy adults, no kidney harm was found.
Taking creatine? Tell me before a blood test.
Kidney problems already? Ask before you take it.
A twelve-week trial found no hair loss.
Your scale jumps? That's water in your muscles from creatine. Not fat!

cta.text: Creatine: know this. The first jump on the scale is mostly water, not fat. Taking it? Tell your doctor before a blood test. Kidney problems? Ask first. Follow MedPeak Health for more health tips that keep you safe.
